_comment: Project-scoped Claude Code settings for the Build Framework. The SessionStart hook auto-loads the read-first orientation files at the start of every session in this repo. The hook is a Node.js script (Claude Code already requires Node, so no extra dependency) and is cross-platform: works on Windows cmd / PowerShell, macOS, Linux, and WSL without bash. The hook reads .claude/read-first-list.txt and obeys the read_first_cap setting in project-config.md.
_permissions_note: Permission fence (calibrated by approval_cadence). The dial that sets how often you review (Maximum / Standard / Minimum) ALSO drives this fence: one question, two effects. The three named profiles live in `_permission_profiles` below — BOOTSTRAP selects ONE at generation (Maximum approval -> maximum_oversight; Standard -> fenced_autonomy [recommended]; Minimum -> sleep_through), copies it into the live `permissions` block, and deletes `_permission_profiles`. The live block below ships the recommended default (fenced_autonomy). Precedence is deny > ask > allow; deny is the hard wall and wins from any scope. The DENY FLOOR IS IDENTICAL across all three profiles — the wall does not move; only the allow/ask split flexes. defaultMode acceptEdits removes file-edit prompts; read-only git (status/diff/log/show/branch) is already auto-approved so it is not listed. git commit/push are ASK on purpose to keep the framework's G1 'no commit without approval' gate alive even under acceptEdits or auto mode. BOOTSTRAP MUST replace the {{...}} placeholders with this project's real commands/manifest (e.g. {{TEST_CMD}} -> 'npm run test *'); until filled, those allow rules simply do not match (less convenient, not unsafe). SECRETS CAVEAT — be honest: deny Read() only blocks Claude's own file tools and recognized bash file commands (cat/head/tail/sed), NOT an arbitrary subprocess (a node/python script that opens the file itself). '.claudeignore' does NOT work. For real secrets use a secret manager / keep them off disk, and enable the sandbox for OS-level enforcement. AUTO MODE: a repo cannot set defaultMode:auto (ignored from project/local settings) — enable it in ~/.claude/settings.json for classifier-backed unattended runs; the deny floor below stays the hard backstop.
_high_risk_approval: Challenge-and-response on high-risk surfaces (the EU AI Act Art. 14 human-oversight control). The fence here is allow/ask/deny only — it CANNOT itself enforce a checklist, so it POINTS at the process artifact: for any RISK-TRIGGER surface (FRAMEWORK-CONFIG §4.19 — destructive data ops / archive-restore-extraction / untrusted-metadata FS writes / credentials / generated-untrusted-HTML / installers-updaters), the approver fills `HIGH-RISK-APPROVAL-CHECKLIST.md` (intent · data lineage · permissions chain · blast radius · rollback plan) BEFORE approving — a bare yes is not enough. This is ADDED rigor on high-stakes surfaces, NOT a replacement for the ask: git commit/push stay `ask` in every profile (G1), the deny floor still walls off secrets + irreversible Bash, and the three honest caveats (CLAUDE.md §6.5) still hold — the checklist closes the JUDGMENT gap, not a technical one. It does NOT fire for a change with no declared trigger (don't make a Lite project's checklist a doc typo).

maximum_oversight._for: approval_cadence: Maximum — tight leash; review most actions. Novice / sensitive / learning.

fenced_autonomy._for: approval_cadence: Standard — approve what you'd approve anyway; routine reversible work runs unattended. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT.

sleep_through._for: approval_cadence: Minimum — wake to finished work. Same repo-set allow/ask as fenced (auto can't be repo-set); pair with the USER-LEVEL `auto` opt-in documented in the generated CLAUDE.md. Trusted direction, long unattended runs.

_receipts_note: Build-receipt capture (M20.6.B). ONE shared lifecycle adapter, node .claude/hooks/receipts-lifecycle.cjs, is registered on every lifecycle boundary below (extend-not-fork). It is ADDED ALONGSIDE the SessionStart read-first hook and the UserPromptSubmit mode-check (a second command in the same group), and its PreToolUse entry is a NEW broad-matcher (.*) group BESIDE the edit-scoped red-gate (riding the red-gate matcher would drop tool_started for Bash/Read/Grep). EXIT-CODE DISCIPLINE (RCPT-09): the adapter has exactly one exit (0) and writes no stdout, so a metrics fault can never change a hook's exit (a Stop exit-2 forces continuation; a UserPromptSubmit exit-2 erases the prompt) — instrumentation failure surfaces as an incomplete interval, never a blocked session. Raw events go to .claude/receipts/ (gitignored); the privacy allowlist (scripts/lib/receipts.cjs) is the mechanism — no prompt text, no paths, no tool arguments, no tool names, ever.
